title: FlashAttention-2: Tensor Cores, loop interchange and warp partitioning

steps.title: S = Q·Kᵀ: Q stays in registers, mma computes the S fragment of one K block
Non-causal FA2: online softmax in registers, P used directly as the A operand, V read with ldmatrix.trans
Causal: skip K blocks above the diagonal, mask only the diagonal blocks

cases.name: n1
cases.purpose: N=1: one Q block and one K block, each with only 1 valid row. O = V, LSE = scale·q·k. Padding rows must be zero-filled, and padding keys must be masked.

cases.name: one_block
cases.purpose: N=64 is exactly one K block, B>1, H>1: checks the mapping from (q block, head, batch) to CTA and the [B,N,H,D] row stride H·D.

cases.name: short_tail
cases.purpose: N=37 < 64, D=128: the 27 padding keys in the block must be masked; with D=128 a row spans two 128-byte swizzle segments.

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: N=300 is not a multiple of the block size: the last Q block and the last K/V block are both partial.

cases.name: peaked_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16, large logits, N=513 is one more than a multiple of the block: the maximum changes in later blocks, and the old O and l must be scaled by 2^(m_old−m_new).

cases.name: scale
cases.purpose: scale=1 instead of 1/√D, logits in the hundreds: scale must come from p.scale; not subtracting the maximum overflows.

cases.name: peaked
cases.purpose: D=128, several blocks, large logits: the maximum is updated repeatedly.

cases.name: uniform
cases.purpose: Q=0: O is the mean of V, LSE = ln(N). Missing the quad reduction of l (adding only this thread's 1/4) gives ln(N/4).

cases.name: ones_v
cases.purpose: V=1: O must equal 1. Dividing by l the wrong number of times, or using different exponents for l and P, moves it away from 1.

cases.name: position
cases.purpose: V[j]=j/N: P fragments in the wrong columns or wrong ldmatrix.trans addresses for V give clearly wrong position values.

cases.name: medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=128: a full inner loop over 16 K blocks.

cases.name: medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=64, FP16: the configuration where each warp owns two 16-row tiles.

cases.name: causal_n1
cases.purpose: Causal with N=1: the only query sees only itself.

cases.name: causal_two_blocks
cases.purpose: Causal, two K blocks, large logits: the mask inside the diagonal block, and the first Q block must not read the second K block.

cases.name: causal_tail
cases.purpose: Causal with N not a multiple of the block: the diagonal mask and the tail mask apply at the same time.

cases.name: causal_position
cases.purpose: Causal, V[j]=j/N, D=128: a mask that is off by one reads a future position value.

cases.name: causal_peaked
cases.purpose: Causal with large logits: masked elements in the diagonal block must not take part in the maximum and must not leave NaN behind.

cases.name: causal_uniform
cases.purpose: Causal with Q=0: O[i] is the mean of V[0..i], LSE[i] = ln(i+1).

cases.name: causal_ones_v
cases.purpose: Causal with V=1: O must equal 1, including row 0, which has only one key.

cases.name: causal_medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=128: each Q block processes only the K blocks on and below the diagonal.

cases.name: causal_medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=64: when a Q block is taller than a K block, the diagonal crosses more than one K block.

cases.name: perf
cases.purpose: B·H=64, N=4096, D=128: 550 GFLOP, Tensor Core throughput and the K/V pipeline.

cases.name: perf_causal
cases.purpose: Same as above but causal: block skipping cuts the work to about half, and the load is unbalanced across Q blocks.

cases.name: perf_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: less compute per key, so the softmax and data movement take a larger share.
